correctness.rationale: The degree constraints partition the graph into degree-3 centers and degree-2 stubs, the latter inducing a perfect matching. Each stub pair joins two distinct centers by a three-edge path or closes a triangle at one center. A cycle/parallel pair in the center skeleton would induce a nonclique biconnected block, so it is a tree with degrees 1 or 3. Its i internal degree-3 vertices and i+2 leaves create 2i+2 centers plus 6i+6 stubs: graph order 8i+8. Deleting skeleton leaves bijects the isomorphism types with subcubic unlabeled trees on i vertices. Degree partition is equitable, with neighbor-count quotient [[0,3],[1,1]], hence joint 1-WL stable histogram, and therefore C² equivalence, depends only on i. First nonisomorphic subcubic trees occur at i=4 (P4 and K1,3), order 40; explicit distinct families persist for every i>=4. Independent networkx unlabeled-tree enumeration gave 1,1,1,1,2,2,4,6,11 for i=0..8.
